title: Printable compound shapes sheet (lesson 61)
subject: Mathematics
source: Seeded from mathematics/y8 lesson 61 (Printable compound shapes sheet (portal worksheet for this lesson))
intro: Lesson 61: Area of compound shapes. To understand how to find the area of compound shapes by splitting them or subtracting simpler shapes

model.title: An L-shaped room is a 10 m by 8 m rectangle with a 4 m by 3 m corner removed. Find its area.
A wall is a rectangle 6 m wide and 4 m high with a triangular top 6 m wide and 2.5 m high. Find its area.
A square tile of side 20 cm has a square hole of side 6 cm. Find the shaded area.

questions.q: A T-shape is a 12 cm by 3 cm bar on top of a 4 cm by 9 cm stem. Find its area.
A 15 m by 10 m rectangle has a 5 m by 4 m rectangle removed. Find the remaining area.

(a) an L-shape: a 9 cm by 7 cm rectangle with a 4 cm by 3 cm corner removed (b) an 8 m by 5 m rectangle with a trapezium on top (parallel sides 8 m and 4 m, height 3 m) (c) a 20 m by 12 m garden with a triangular pond (base 6 m, height 4 m): area of grass (d) an arrow: a 10 cm by 4 cm rectangle with a triangle of base 8 cm and height 5 cm at one end
Turf costs £4.50 per m². How much does it cost to turf the grass in (c)?
A window is a 1.2 m by 0.8 m rectangle with a triangle of height 0.3 m on its 1.2 m top. Glass costs £35 per m². Find the cost.
A shape of 50 cm² has a hole of 8 cm². The shaded area is:
The first step for a compound shape?
questions.a: split it (or plan to subtract) and find the missing lengths

questions.q: Big question: do different ways of splitting give the same area?
questions.a: Yes: area does not change when we cut it up differently; choose the quickest way.
